html:
The Macuxi, or Makushi, are a Carib-speaking people of the savannas where Brazil, Guyana and Venezuela meet, mostly in the Brazilian state of Roraima. Their land reaches to Mount Roraima, which in their stories is the stump of a great tree that once held all the world's fruits.

They grow cassava, fish, and over the centuries took up cattle raising. The Hallelujah religion began among them in the 1840s and spread to the Akawaio and other neighbours. In the 1900s ranchers and rice farmers moved onto their savannas. After a long campaign, Brazil in 2005 recognised the Raposa Serra do Sol territory, which they share with the Wapishana and others, and in 2009 its Supreme Court upheld it and ordered the farmers out. See Brazil and Guyana.
